Filtration and sampling equipment was soaked in 10% bleach for at least 6 hours between each filtration run or sampling; filtration lines were primed with 10% bleach for 15 minutes, then flushed three times with Milli-Q water.
Water was stored at 4 °C and filtered within 12 hours of collection through 47 mm, 0.45 µm mixed cellulose ester membranes with a peristaltic pump; filters were stored at -80 °C.

Lowest common ancestor (LCA) script in eDNAFlow (Mousavi-Derazmahalleh et al. 2021): where an ASV had several top hits within 1% similarity of each other (Diff = 1), its taxonomy was collapsed to their lowest common ancestor.
BLASTn with at most 20 target sequences, on CSIRO's Petrichor HPC cluster. A species-level assignment required at least 98% identity and 100% query coverage.

The distribution of each species was checked in Fishes of Australia (https://fishesofaustralia.net.au/); taxa not expected in south-east Australia were assigned to genus or higher, based on related species in the area.
Only fish ASVs were curated and kept in the final table.

Fish ASVs were curated by hand. Species assignments below 98.5% identity were changed to genus where congeneric species with no reference sequence occur in the region. Good matches (above 97%) with poor taxonomic resolution were checked for errors in the reference database. Large groups of ASVs assigned to one family or genus (such as Myctophidae or Urolophus) were split into clusters differing by more than 2% on a distance-based tree, each with its own name (Urolophus Sp1, Urolophus Sp2). Chimeric sequences and rare variants close to common ASVs were removed.
